name: View update
first: SwiftUI running a view's body again when a value that the body read changes, and not when a value it did not read changes.

dependsOn.why: The example changes state, one of the values that make SwiftUI run a body again.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `taps` and `visits` are state properties, as `taps` is in `Counter` on the page of State.

dependsOn.why: The example changes its state in the closure of a modifier that runs when a view appears.
dependsOn.whyInExample: `onAppear` is a modifier of each `Text`, whose closure changes the state.

what.is: A view update is SwiftUI running a view's `body` again, to get a new description of the view. SwiftUI does it when a value that `body` read the last time it ran changes, such as a state property. A change to a value that `body` did not read does not run it again.
what.afterExample: Both views change a state property when they appear. Only `Counter` reads its state in `body`, so only the `body` of `Counter` runs a second time.
what.problem: A screen must show the newest data, but running every view's `body` after every change would do work that changes nothing. SwiftUI runs again only the bodies that read what changed.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that when a state value changes, SwiftUI updates the parts of the view hierarchy that depend on it. A `body` depends on the values it read when it last ran. Here, `body` of `Welcome` never read `visits`, so its change ran nothing, while `body` of `Counter` read `taps`, so its change ran that `body` again.

when.text: Use it to keep updates small: read in `body` only the values that the view shows, and give each view inside it only the values that it needs.
Don't count on `body` running a set number of times. SwiftUI runs it whenever it needs a new description, so `body` should not do work with effects, such as saving data.

parts.name: The value `taps`, read on line 17
parts.text: The `body` of `Counter` reads `taps` on lines 17 and 18, so `taps` is a value that this `body` depends on. The `body` of `Welcome` never reads `visits`, so it does not depend on `visits`.

steps.text: Line 25 makes a `Welcome` and a renderer for it, and line 26 asks for its image, so SwiftUI draws it.
The `body` of `Welcome` runs, and line 6 prints {{Welcome body runs}}.
The `Text` appears, and line 9 adds 1 to `visits`. The `body` did not read `visits`, so SwiftUI does not run it again.
Line 27 makes a `Counter` and a renderer for it, and line 28 asks for its image.
The `body` of `Counter` runs, and line 17 reads `taps` and prints {{Counter body runs: 0}}.
The `Text` appears, and line 20 adds 1 to `taps`, which the `body` read.
A value that the `body` read changed, so SwiftUI runs it again, and line 17 prints {{Counter body runs: 1}}.

end.text: SwiftUI ran a `body` again only when a value it had read changed: `taps`, and not `visits`.
